name: lidded-box
why: The seeded two-body part, and the one the field case asks about: a base of 48000 - 56·36·18 = 11712 mm³ and a lid of 7200 + 55.4·35.4·4 = 15044.64 mm³, never fused. The lip is drawn 0.3 mm inside the pocket and the lid stands 0.5 above the rim, so the closest the two come is 0.3 mm — the number a reader of the script gets wrong by quoting the standoff. The base's rim is not a patch of the bed: the part stands on the base's whole 2400 mm² underside alone.
